name: Alienware m17 R5 zones
notes: Unverified: never tried on this machine. Written on 2026-10-16 by alienfx.mjs from alienfx-tools, https://github.com/T-Troll/alienfx-tools, MIT licence, commit 3289c320 (2026-10-14): alienfx-gui/Mappings/devices.csv, each machine's map of its lights.
Its map there: “Alienware m17R5”, line 590, device “Tron lights”. Which id lights what is that map's; the names are its own, in plain words.
The protocol is verified: the AW-ELC's live preview, as alienware-17-r5-zones.json sends it, which stores nothing in the device.

Matched on the machine (#326): SMBIOS names it “Alienware m17 R5 AMD”, as dmidecode reports it in linuxhw/DMI, https://github.com/linuxhw/DMI (CC BY 4.0), commit 57b21bc6 (2025-01-06): Notebook/Alienware/m17/m17 R5 AMD, SKU 0B5D; the m17 R5 is sold in that edition only.
Left out: id 0, “Left of Tron”, which alienfx-tools marks as the power button: the firmware drives it, as on the m18 R1.
alienfx-tools does not mark id 2, “Power button”, as the power button: it is drawn, as the 17 R5's is.
alienfx-tools marks id 3, “AlienHead”, as an indicator, which it keeps dark when the lights are off; here it follows the effect.
alienfx-tools names id 2 the power button yet marks id 0 as one: which of the two the firmware keeps, only the machine can say.

Drawn from the front, lid open, the lights at the back seen through the hinge. Where a light sits is not in the source: the keyboard zones keep the order and widths of alienfx-tools' grid, the rest is drawn where its name puts it.
